Mitra to Fedify gateway delivery
================================

This fixture records Mitra v5.10.0 delivering a portable `Create` to a Fedify
inbox. The unmodified image was pinned to
`codeberg.org/silverpill/mitra@sha256:4348ddea1d819f654cd3e6be4e955b3933d1d21807c6a9a8ef64eda4333f1d0a`.
Its version output was `mitra 5.10.0`; tag `v5.10.0` points to source commit
`17340ef09d4a902f301acdcfde094f5778d72f35`.

The Fedify scratch client created the portable actor and the DID-signed
`Note` and `Create`, then submitted the activity to Mitra's gateway outbox.
Mitra's delivery worker forwarded it to
`https://fedify.example:18444/users/alice/inbox`, signing the HTTP request
with Mitra's RSA gateway key. The original `eddsa-jcs-2022` proofs on the
activity and note were generated by Fedify's client and retained by Mitra.
This capture verifies Mitra's transport of client-signed portable objects;
it does not establish independent DID-proof generation by Mitra.

Fedify separately called `verifyRequestDetailed()` on the original request
and accepted its Cavage HTTP Signature with the normal current-time
freshness check. The signing key ID was the actor's compatible identifier
on the Mitra gateway with `#main-key`. Mitra's signed components were
`(request-target)`, `host`, `date`, and `digest`.

Fedify's inbox then returned HTTP 202 and dispatched the `Create` listener
with the expected activity and actor IDs. The inbox authenticated the
activity's DID proof and skipped HTTP Signature verification. HTTP 202 and
listener dispatch therefore establish proof-authenticated receipt; the
separate verification result establishes acceptance of the gateway HTTP
Signature.

The request body and headers were captured directly at the Fedify receiver.
The actor document was fetched from Mitra while resolving the HTTP signing
key. Neither the request nor that response was reconstructed from fixture
objects. The capture time, source pins, hashes, response, and listener result
are recorded alongside the original bodies. Private keys, database files,
and invite codes are excluded.


Capture procedure and limits
----------------------------

The capture used the registered actor from the [Fedify to Mitra setup].
Gateway registration and the actor `Update` used a scratch FEP-ae97 client,
compact signing contexts, and Fedify's existing internal outgoing normalizer.
The compact setup contexts avoided Mitra's limit of 20 recursively
counted embedded JSON objects. Fedify does not provide a public FEP-ae97
client; this delivery is not evidence of one.

Mitra and PostgreSQL 16 ran locally in Podman. Mitra's listener was
`http://127.0.0.1:18497`; gateway support was enabled and SSRF protection
was disabled for the local capture. The Fedify receiver used HTTPS on
`127.0.0.1:18444` with a certificate signed by a local CA trusted by Mitra's
OS CA store. Certificate verification remained enabled. These settings do
not establish public deployment behavior.

To repeat the delivery, complete the registered-actor setup described in the
linked fixture, then:

1.  Run a Fedify HTTPS receiver with a `Person` at */users/alice*, its inbox
    at */users/alice/inbox*, and a `Create` listener that records activity
    and actor IDs. Capture incoming bodies and headers before consuming them.
2.  Sign a native `Note` and `Create` with the registered actor's DID key.
    Address both to `https://fedify.example:18444/users/alice` and submit the
    activity to the actor's compatible outbox on Mitra using the same compact
    setup contexts and normalization described in the linked fixture.
3.  Let Mitra's delivery worker send the request. Independently verify its
    HTTP Signature on a request clone, then pass the original request to
    `federation.fetch()`. Record the HTTP verification result, inbox response,
    listener record, and exact fetched signing-key actor document.

Fresh identities and proofs produce different IDs, signatures, and hashes.
Offline replay uses the captured time for a separate strict HTTP signature
freshness check. The inbox replay disables HTTP timestamp validation for the
stored request; it does not recreate Mitra's worker. The live capture used the
normal current-time check.
Run the offline regressions with:

~~~~ bash
mise run test:deno packages/fedify/src/sig/mitra-receive-interop.test.ts
~~~~

Mastodon interoperability is outside this result.

[Fedify to Mitra setup]: ../send/README.md
